title: Fix: prevent profile mismatch when model reloads across GPU pools; add regression test
author: Ethan Park
description: Context: With the hardware tuning profile pack enabled, we’ve seen a rare but high-impact scenario where a model is unloaded/evicted and later reloaded on a different GPU pool (e.g., H100 -> L40S, or pool A -> pool B with different driver/CUDA). The model reload path was reusing a cached ActiveProfile computed at initial load time, which could result in the runtime applying kernel/scheduler/KV-cache knobs intended for the previous pool. This is subtle (no immediate crash in most cases) but can cause unexpected tail latency, increased kernel fallbacks, and in a few cases lower memory headroom than the new SKU supports. Root cause: ModelManager cached the selected profile keyed only by model_id (and profile pack version), but not by the hardware identity / pool fingerprint. On reload, the selection step was skipped if a cached profile existed, even when the backing GPU pool changed. Fix: Make profile selection explicitly tied to a HardwareFingerprint (sku + device class + driver + cuda runtime + pool_id), and require recomputation on model load when the fingerprint differs. Add a defensive guardrail: if the cached profile_id does not match the newly-selected profile_id, we now emit a structured warning log and increment a counter, then proceed with the newly-selected profile. Also add a regression test that simulates model reload across two pools with different SKUs and asserts the runtime selects the correct profile each time. Notes: This does not change default profile selection rules; it only ensures they are applied deterministically on every model load. It is safe for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Testing: unit tests for fingerprinting + cache invalidation; new regression test in runtime/tests/profiles_model_reload.rs; ran benchmark-lab smoke locally on H100 + L40S configs (no perf deltas expected). Rollout: no special rollout required; this is correctness and should reduce risk during canaries / mixed fleet upgrades.
commits: runtime/profiles: include pool + driver/cuda in HardwareFingerprint
model_manager: recompute profile on model load when fingerprint changes
metrics: add profile_mismatch_on_reload_total counter + structured log
tests: add regression test for reload across pools with different SKU
changed_areas: Serving runtime: profile selection + caching behavior
Model lifecycle: model reload path and hardware-aware invalidation
Observability: counter + log for mismatch detection
Tests: regression coverage for cross-pool reload
snippet: Before: cached_profile = profile_cache.get(model_id) && skip selection; After: fp = HardwareFingerprint::detect(ctx); cached = profile_cache.get((model_id, fp)); if cached missing or fp differs -> selector.select(ctx) and update cache; if previous cached exists for model_id with different fp -> log warning + metrics::profile_mismatch_on_reload_total++
review_conversation: Noah Patel (review): Can we make sure the cache key change doesn’t accidentally blow up memory usage? Model IDs can be high-cardinality; adding pool_id could multiply entries.

Ethan Park (author): Good call. I changed the cache to retain only the most recent fingerprint per model_id and explicitly evict the old entry on mismatch (so we don’t keep unbounded (model_id, fp) pairs). Added a small unit test to verify eviction semantics.
Quentin Harris (review): Please add a metric for when this happens; it’ll be useful to validate whether we’re hitting this in the wild during 1.22 rollout.

Ethan Park (author): Added profile_mismatch_on_reload_total with labels {sku_from, sku_to, profile_version}. Also made the log structured with model_id + pool_id for correlating with scheduler_queue_ms spikes.
Omar El-Sayed (review): One concern: if a customer pins profile_version, are we guaranteed to re-select within that version on reload? The test should cover pinned versions too.
Ethan Park (author): Updated regression test to pin profile_version=1.22.0-pack. It now asserts we still switch profile_id as SKU changes, but remain within the pinned pack version.
Sean Gallagher (review): Please confirm behavior is non-fatal. We should not fail model loads just because a cache entry existed with the wrong profile.
Ethan Park (author): Confirmed: we always proceed with the newly-selected profile, and the guardrail is observability-only. No load failures introduced.
Noah Patel (approval): Looks good with eviction. Thanks for adding the metric; this will help SRE validate rollouts.
Quentin Harris (approval): Approved. Regression test is solid and matches the reported failure mode.
merge_summary: Merged as 1 commit into main. Cherry-pick candidate for runtime-1.22 release branch if any late canary anomalies show up; otherwise will ride the next train.
release_notes: Fixes a correctness issue where a model could reuse a cached hardware tuning profile after reloading onto a different GPU pool; adds a mismatch counter and regression test.
